headline: The questions you ask determine the answers you find
universal_truth: Questions are more powerful than answers—they direct where minds go
fun_facts: Einstein said if he had an hour to solve a problem, he'd spend 55 minutes defining the question
Open-ended questions activate more brain regions than yes/no questions
The Socratic method—teaching through questions—is over 2,400 years old and still works
discussion_questions: What question would most change your life if you found the answer?
What questions are you afraid to ask—and why?
How could you ask better questions in your daily conversations?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Einstein said if he had one hour to save the world, he'd spend 55 minutes defining the problem and 5 minutes solving it. The quality of your questions determines the quality of your answers—and ultimately, the quality of your life.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We're taught to find answers. But the most powerful thinking skill might be asking better questions. What makes a question 'good'? Why do some questions open doors while others hit walls?

options.text: It opens up new possibilities and directions
options.response: Yes. Great questions expand thinking; weak questions constrain it.

options.text: It's specific enough to be answerable
options.response: Specificity helps, but the best questions do something more...

q1.title: The 55-Minute Rule
q1.script: Einstein, Darwin, and Newton all emphasized question-framing over answer-finding. A poorly framed question leads to useless answers. A well-framed question often reveals its own answer. The hard work is in the asking.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The 55-Minute Rule"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Open vs. Closed
q2.script: Yes-or-no questions shut down thinking. Open questions—'how might we...,' 'what would happen if...'—activate more brain regions and generate more creative responses. The structure of your question shapes the structure of possible answers.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Socrates Knew
q3.script: 2,400 years ago, Socrates taught by asking questions, not giving answers. He believed truth emerged through inquiry. This 'Socratic method' is still used in law schools and philosophy departments because questions force deeper thinking than lectures.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Instead of seeking answers, become a collector of better questions. 'Why?' is good. 'How might I?' is better. 'What would make this easy?' is powerful. Your questions determine your direction.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 26. Tomorrow, we'll explore how imagination works. Until then, ask one question you've been avoiding—and see what opens up.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Question Upgrade - Better Inquiries
growTrack.learning_objective: Improve the quality of questions you ask
growTrack.activity: Take a problem you're facing and write down the question you've been asking about it. Then reframe it three different ways—make it broader, make it more specific, make it about possibility. Notice which reframe feels most useful.
